A reads as a finished LinkedIn piece: a bold '9 of them broke zero rules. So are those nine safe? Not proven.' hook, a per-category grid of all 319 replies, a 20-run simulation where 5 runs come out perfect, the (1-rate)^29 curve with 56%/23%/5% markers, the Wilson-interval scene, and a takeaway card ('Zero out of 29 rules out a habit. It doesn't rule out a slip.'). It also has a break-rate slider that gives exact probabilities (1% -> 75%, 12% -> 2.5%). B is the more interactive lesson: tap a row to see each model's breakdown, a guess quiz that answers 'Not quite' or 'Right', and rate buttons that animate clean-by-luck tests. But it is a dark multi-step web widget with a 7-step pager, which is harder to carry into a LinkedIn post than A's self-playing 60 s card. Craft problems on both sides are minor, so fit for the stated LinkedIn use decided it, narrowly.
